title: Local Card Grading Services (2026)
verdict: Local card grading services are mostly submission middlemen, and AGS is the exception worth checking: it takes drop-offs at select locations and grades in-house.

Graders centralize because the equipment and the security are expensive. PSA, CGC and Beckett each run a small number of sites. So the useful questions are how fast the cards come back and whether you can skip the shipping leg.

list: Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.
Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.

why: You are not limited to the mailbox. AGS lists in-person drop-off at select locations and secure intake at its Staten Island headquarters, and it operates satellite labs. Ask AGS which site is taking cards before you set out.
There is not much to it. Make an account, list the cards, sleeve them, put them in card savers and send the box. AGS confirms the order, grades it and ships it back with tracking.

Standard turnaround is 20 business days or less. The faster bulk tiers come back in 10 business days at $20 and 5 at $30, and AGS says same-day grading is available for urgent submissions. A scan that takes under 10 seconds is what makes those numbers possible.

faq.q: Are there local card grading services?
faq.a: There is rarely a grader in town. You can mail cards to a grader, drop them at a select AGS location, hand them to a card shop that forwards them for a fee, or find a grader at a card show.

faq.q: Is mailing cards for grading safe?
faq.a: Yes, if you pack them properly and use a tracked, insured service. AGS returns cards with tracking and offers optional insurance on the return shipment.

faq.q: How should I pack cards for grading?
faq.a: Put each card in a new penny sleeve, then a semi-rigid card saver. Sandwich the stack between cardboard, wrap it in bubble wrap and box it. Top loaders are allowed, but card savers travel better.
Rarely. Many act as middlemen: they collect cards, batch them, send them to a grading company and add a handling fee. Ask which grader they use, which tier, and what the total will be.

faq.q: How do I submit cards to AGS?
faq.a: Create an account at agscard.com, fill out the submission form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. You can also drop off at select AGS locations. The dashboard tracks the order.
